test_title: PYST 48: RRB Group D - Mathematics (Held On: 17 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: maths
question: In a student body election, 5% of the eligible voters are aged 18–21 years, 12% are aged 21–25 years, and the rest are older than 25 years. Among these groups, 80% of the 18–21 year age group and 60% of the 21–25 year age group actually voted. If the number of voters aged 21–25 years who voted exceeds those aged 18–21 years by 320, what is the difference between the number of eligible voters aged 18–21 years and those aged 21–25 years?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let total voters = x

18–21 voters = 5% ⇒ 0.05x, voted = 80% ⇒ 0.04x

21–25 voters = 12% ⇒ 0.12x, voted = 60% ⇒ 0.072x

Difference in voters = 0.072x − 0.04x = 0.032x = 320

x = 10000

Difference in eligible voters = 12% − 5% = 7% of x = 700

**∴ Answer = 700**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

18–21 group = 5%, voting = 80%

21–25 group = 12%, voting = 60%

Difference in voters = 320

**Formula used:**

Actual voters = Total × % × voting rate

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let total eligible voters = x

⇒ 18–21 voters who voted = 0.05x × 0.8 = 0.04x

⇒ 21–25 voters who voted = 0.12x × 0.6 = 0.072x

⇒ Difference = 0.072x − 0.04x = 0.032x

⇒ 0.032x = 320 ⇒ x = 10000

⇒ Eligible voters (difference) = (0.12x − 0.05x) = 0.07x

⇒ = 0.07 × 10000 = 700

**∴ The correct answer is 700.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Conversion

Convert % into decimal for calculation

Layered Percentage

Apply percentage on percentage stepwise

Difference Concept

Find total using given difference

Key Insight

Solve for total first, then required difference
